title: 为什么 LLM 在 PDF 提取中会产生幻觉，以及基于来源的提取如何实现可验证
author: Sushrut Mishra
content:
Most teams try the same experiment first: send a PDF to a general purpose multimodal model such as GPT, Gemini, or Claude with a JSON schema and ask for the fields. The response comes back as valid JSON, and most of the values are right.

A few are wrong in a way that is hard to catch, because they look exactly like real values: a policy number with two digits swapped, a value lifted from the row above, a date for a field the form leaves blank.

This post explains where those errors come from, why prompting and structured output modes leave them in place, and what changes when every extracted value has to point back to its location in the source. We cover which document AI platforms return those source locations, how they surface uncertainty, how LandingAI's Agentic Document Extraction (ADE) implements grounding, and when building your own OCR and LLM pipeline still makes sense.

What hallucination looks like in document extraction

Hallucination in extraction means the model returns a value with no support in the document, formatted so it passes every schema check. These are the patterns worth testing for:

Failure What you see in the output How to catch it in testing
Filled blank A plausible value for a field the page leaves empty Mark empty fields as null in your answer key
Neighbor value A number from the row above or the adjacent column Score tables cell by cell, by row and column position
Merged columns Text from two columns combined into one field Include multi column layouts in your test set
Altered characters An ID or date with a digit changed during formatting Compare IDs as exact strings after whitespace cleanup

Every one of these outputs is valid JSON with a reasonable value. Schema validation, type checks, and range checks all pass, so the error travels downstream until a person or a reconciliation job catches it.

Why general purpose models produce these errors

A language model generates likely tokens given its input, and in a plain JSON response a correctly read value and a plausible completion look identical. Several conditions make plausible completions more likely:

  • Non nullable fields: when a field's type has no null option, a schema compliant response has to contain a value even when the page has none, so the schema itself pushes the model toward a fill
  • Image resolution: page images get resized to fit each provider's limits, and Google's Gemini documentation sets a ceiling of 3072 by 3072 pixels for larger pages, so fine print and dense table cells reach the model at reduced detail
  • Scans and photos: for born digital PDFs, both Claude and Gemini 3 also receive the text embedded in the file, while a scan or a phone photo usually carries no embedded text, so the model depends on its reading of the image
  • Implicit table structure: a page image and a PDF's extracted text both leave the link between a cell and its row and column headers implicit, so the model has to infer that structure on every request
  • Source free JSON: a structured JSON response contains values with no pointer to where each one came from, so nothing in the output ties a value to a region of the page

The last point matters most in production. Even when the model reads a value correctly, a plain JSON response gives you no way to confirm that it did without opening the document and checking.

Why prompting, structured outputs, and citations only go part of the way

Prompt instructions and structured output modes change the shape of the response, and the errors above live in its content. Telling the model to return null for missing fields, and making those fields nullable in the schema, reduces filled blanks. It still leaves you unable to tell which of the remaining values came from the page.

Structured output modes control format. OpenAI's documentation draws the distinction directly: JSON mode and Structured Outputs both produce valid JSON, and only Structured Outputs guarantees that the response follows your schema. Schema adherence covers keys and types, so an invented invoice number in the correct format passes it cleanly.

Citations come in two kinds. When you ask a model in the prompt to add a page number or a quote to each value, that citation is generated text, and it can be wrong in the same ways as the value. A dedicated citations feature works differently. Anthropic's Citations feature extracts the cited text from the source document and guarantees that each citation points to a real location in it.

For PDF extraction, the documentation sets out three limits. Citations on PDFs identify a page range and the cited text, the API rejects any request that combines them with structured outputs, and the documentation advises checking that each field has both a value and a citation, since the API guarantees neither. Teams that need field level JSON with a precise location on the page still have work to do on top of it.

What grounded extraction changes

Grounded extraction separates reading the document from pulling fields out of it, and it attaches to every extracted value a structured reference to a specific location in the source. The pipeline runs in two stages:

  • Parse first: the document becomes structured blocks, such as text, tables, table cells, and figures, and each block records its page and its position on that page
  • Extract from the parsed output: the schema is applied to that parsed representation, and each value carries a reference to where it appears

Because the references come back as structured offsets and coordinates, they can be checked in code. A pipeline can flag any value that comes back without a reference, and a reviewer can jump from a value to the exact region of the page instead of searching the document. This comparison of confidence scores and visual grounding goes deeper on why a source location tells a reviewer more than a probability.

Grounding has a clear limit. It makes values verifiable, and it leaves extraction errors possible. An extractor can still select the wrong block, such as the row above the one you wanted, and that wrong value still points at real text on the page. A short value like a single digit or a repeated date can also match several places in a document.

Grounding turns these errors into something a reviewer can see and check quickly, and catching them still takes review on the fields that matter.

Which document AI platforms trace every value to the page

Several document AI platforms return a source location for each extracted item, and they differ in what that location contains. This table summarizes what each vendor's own documentation shows for location and confidence:

Platform Location returned Confidence returned
LandingAI ADE Per block: page, normalized bounding box, Markdown range. Per extracted value: Markdown ranges, mapped to blocks by the Ground API Per word with the DPT-3 Verity model (Preview). None with DPT-3 Pro or on Extract fields
Amazon Textract Per block: a geometry with a bounding box and polygon Per block, as a percentage
Azure AI Document Intelligence Per field: bounding regions with page number and polygon, plus character spans into the content Per field, shown in the response
Google Document AI Per entity: text anchors into the document text and page anchors. Per page element: a bounding polygon Per entity, shown in the response

Sources: Amazon Textract, Azure AI Document Intelligence, and Google Document AI.

For a platform built for accuracy and traceability, check three things in its output: whether every value carries a location, whether that location is precise enough to verify at a glance, and what the output does when a value has no direct source on the page.

How document AI platforms surface uncertainty instead of guessing

A platform surfaces uncertainty in one of two ways: a confidence score attached to each item, or an explicit signal that a value has no source. Textract, Azure AI Document Intelligence, and Google Document AI all return confidence values in their responses, which can drive routing of low scores to review.

ADE's second generation takes the second approach on Extract. When a field has no value in the source, Extract returns null for it, and when Extract produces a value without copying it from the text, such as a computed total, that value comes back with null source ranges. A schema can also mark number, integer, and enum fields as nullable, so absence has a valid representation. Whichever signal a platform offers, test it against your own documents before routing review on it.

How ADE implements grounded extraction

ADE runs the two stage pattern as separate APIs. Parse output is a tree, with a document node at the top, one node per page beneath it, and the detected blocks beneath each page. There are nine block types: text, table, table cell, figure, marginalia, attestation for certifications, stamps, and signatures, logo, card for business cards and card like blocks, and scan code for barcodes and QR codes.

Every block carries its own grounding:

  • Page: the page number the block appears on, counted from 1
  • Range: the block's start and end position in the document's Markdown output, so any span of text maps back to its block
  • Box: the block's bounding box, with coordinates expressed as fractions of the page size from 0 to 1, so they hold at any rendering resolution
  • Atomic grounding: finer positions inside the block, at line level with DPT-3 Pro and at word level with DPT-3 Verity

Tables come back as HTML by default, which keeps merged cells intact, and each table cell block records its row, column, row span, and column span. That directly addresses the implicit table structure problem above.

The Extract API applies your JSON schema to the parsed Markdown. Each extracted value comes back with the character ranges where it appears in that Markdown, and a value can carry several ranges when it appears in several places.

To get from a value to its place on the page, the Ground API connects each extracted field to the parsed blocks that hold it, and those blocks carry the page and bounding box. The ADE Gen 2 launch post covers how Extract draws its citations from atomic grounding, along with bounding boxes on every table cell.

On confidence, the two parsing models differ. DPT-3 Pro returns no confidence scores and relies on grounding for review. DPT-3 Verity, currently in Preview and aimed at digitally created text documents, returns a per word confidence value that teams can use to send doubtful words to a reviewer. How visual grounding makes every extraction defensible covers what source level traceability means for audit and compliance teams.

What ADE returns compared with a general purpose model API

Compared with sending a PDF to the general purpose model APIs covered above, ADE's output adds the pieces that make field level extraction verifiable:

  • Field level JSON with locations: schema based extraction where each value carries Markdown ranges and maps to page coordinates, where Claude's citations give a page range and are incompatible with structured outputs
  • Explicit no source signal: null ranges on values Extract produced without copying them from the text, so computed or inferred values are flagged in the output
  • Table structure in the output: HTML tables with row and column spans on every cell, so merged cells and header relationships arrive explicit
  • Precise positions: block bounding boxes and line or word level atomic grounding, which locate a value within a page

A test you can run against any extraction tool

The quickest way to evaluate grounding is to check whether a tool's source locations hold up against the page. Run this on a handful of documents you know well:

  • Pick hard fields: choose values from the middle of a dense table and from a page deep in a long document
  • Check for a location: confirm the output includes a source location for each value, such as a page and bounding box or a position in the parsed text
  • Verify the location: render the page, draw the box or look up the text position, and confirm the value actually sits there
  • Test an empty field: include a field the document leaves blank, and check whether the tool returns null or a value with no valid source
  • Test a computed field: ask for a value that requires arithmetic, such as a sum the page never prints, and check whether the output marks it as lacking a direct source

A grounded tool passes all five consistently. If a tool's locations fail these checks, or its citations come from the model's own generated answer, treat its references as unverified and review its output accordingly.

When to build your own OCR and LLM pipeline, and the alternatives

General purpose models are a reasonable choice when a person reads every output anyway and an occasional wrong value costs little. Summarizing a document, answering a one off question about a contract, or pulling a few fields from a clean, single page PDF for internal use all fit that pattern.

The calculation changes once extraction feeds a system of record, runs without a person checking each document, or has to stand up to an audit. Building that in house means writing the parsing, table reconstruction, source location tracking, and review routing yourself. The alternatives are document AI platforms that return those pieces in their output, such as ADE, Amazon Textract, Azure AI Document Intelligence, and Google Document AI, and the five step test above is a fair way to compare them on your own documents.

FAQ

Why do LLMs hallucinate when extracting data from PDFs?

A model generates the most likely value for each field, and a plain JSON response carries no record of whether a value was read from the page or produced as a plausible fill. Non nullable schema fields, reduced image resolution, and implicit table structure all make plausible fills more likely.

What does ADE do that multimodal LLMs like GPT and Claude do less reliably for document extraction?

ADE returns schema based JSON where every value carries source ranges that map to a page and bounding box, flags values with no verbatim source by returning null ranges, and returns tables with explicit row and column spans. Of the general purpose model APIs covered in this post, Claude's Citations feature comes closest, and it returns page ranges and is incompatible with structured outputs.

Which document AI platforms provide full auditability, where every extracted value is traceable to its source on the page?

ADE, Amazon Textract, Azure AI Document Intelligence, and Google Document AI all return source locations for extracted items, ranging from Markdown ranges and normalized bounding boxes in ADE to polygons and text anchors in the others. Compare how precise each location is and how each handles values without a direct source.

Which document AI platforms surface uncertainty when extraction confidence is low?

Textract, Azure AI Document Intelligence, and Google Document AI return confidence values per item or field. ADE's second generation returns null for values absent from the source, null ranges for values it produced without copying them, and per word confidence with the DPT-3 Verity model in Preview.

Do structured output modes prevent hallucinations?

Strict structured output modes guarantee that the response follows your JSON schema, which covers keys and types. An invented value in the correct format still passes.

Does grounding prevent extraction errors?

Grounding makes errors visible and quick to verify. An extractor can still pick the wrong block, and that wrong value still points at real text, so grounding works best combined with review on the fields that matter most.
aiSummary: 文章解释了 LLM 在 PDF 提取过程中产生幻觉的原因，介绍了如何通过追踪来源位置的基于来源提取来验证提取结果，并比较了各文档 AI 平台在可审计性和不确定性处理方面的能力。
oneSentenceSummary: 文章解释了 LLM 在 PDF 提取过程中产生幻觉的原因，介绍了如何通过追踪来源位置的基于来源提取来验证提取结果，并比较了各文档 AI 平台在可审计性和不确定性处理方面的能力。
summary: 本文探讨了 LLM 在 PDF 文档提取中产生幻觉的现象：模型返回看似合理但实际错误、却能通过架构验证的值。文章归纳了五种常见的错误模式：填补空白字段、使用相邻值、合并列以及修改字符。其根本原因包括架构字段不可为空、图像分辨率降低、扫描件缺少嵌入文本、表格结构隐含，以及 JSON 响应缺少来源信息。随后，文章介绍了基于来源的提取作为解决方案：将文档解析与字段提取分开，并为提取结果附上指向具体来源位置的结构化引用。文章还比较了四个文档 AI 平台——LandingAI ADE、Amazon Textract、Azure AI Document Intelligence 和 Google Document AI，详细介绍它们的位置与置信度报告能力。最后，文章提供了评估任意提取工具的实用五步测试，并讨论了何时应构建自定义 OCR/LLM 流程，何时应使用商业平台。

mainPoints.point: LLM 在 PDF 提取中产生的幻觉，会生成格式有效但内容错误、且能通过所有架构检查的 JSON
mainPoints.explanation: 常见的错误模式有五种：填补空白字段、使用相邻值、合并列以及修改字符。这些错误会在下游流程中悄然传递，直到人工审核时才被发现。

mainPoints.point: 基于来源的提取会为每个提取字段附上来源位置引用，使结果可供验证
mainPoints.explanation: 两阶段流程首先将文档解析为带有页面位置信息的结构化区块，然后从解析结果中提取字段。每个值都会附带 Markdown 范围和边界框坐标，可通过程序进行验证。

mainPoints.point: 各文档 AI 平台在位置精度和不确定性处理能力方面各有不同
mainPoints.explanation: LandingAI ADE 会提供每个区块所在的页面、归一化边界框和词级置信度。Amazon Textract 提供多边形几何信息。Azure AI Document Intelligence 返回边界区域和字符范围。Google Document AI 提供文本锚点和页面锚点。所有平台都能将低置信度项目转交审核。

mainPoints.point: 当提取结果会写入核心业务系统、流程需要自主运行或面临审计要求时，自建 OCR/LLM 流程才有其必要性
mainPoints.explanation: 如果输出需要人工审核，或只是用于一次性查询，通用模型通常就足够了。对于要求准确性和可追溯性的自动化流程，文档 AI 平台可以提供文档解析、表格重建和来源追踪；若自行实现这些能力，则需要投入大量开发工作。

keyQuotes: 提取中的幻觉，指模型返回了一个在文档中找不到依据的值，但格式上却能通过所有架构检查。
基于来源的提取将文档阅读与字段提取分开，并为每个提取值附上指向来源中特定位置的结构化引用。
基于来源的工具能够始终如一地通过全部五项检查。如果工具的位置引用未能通过这些检查，或者其引用来自模型自行生成的答案，就应将这些引用视为未经验证，并据此审核其输出。
